The present invention relates to a power transmission device incorporating two or more pistons.

The power transmission device may comprise: a housing configured to define a mounting space through the interconnection of a clutch housing, a clutch connecting portion, a clutch hub, and a disk housing; a power transmission hub selectively and operatively coupled to the housing; a plurality of first friction disks splined to the inner circumferential surface of the disk housing; a plurality of second friction disks splined to the outer circumferential surface of the power transmission hub and arranged in alternating fashion with the first friction disks; a piston module comprising two or more pistons, each associated with a corresponding piston chamber, configured to selectively engage the first friction disks with the second friction disks through frictional coupling upon application of operating hydraulic pressure to the piston chambers; and at least one return spring or separating spring configured to apply a spring load that counteracts the axial force generated by the operating hydraulic pressure, the spring being disposed either inward or outward of the piston module, wherein a friction material is affixed to one or both surfaces of each first friction disk and/or each second friction disk.

# Power Transmission Device with Multi-Piston Friction Disk Engagement System

## Overview

The present invention relates to a power transmission device that employs an innovative dual or multi-piston configuration to control the engagement of friction disks, thereby enabling more precise and efficient power transfer within mechanical or automotive drivetrain systems. This design enhances the reliability and responsiveness of clutch engagement while accommodating varying torque and speed conditions.

## Housing Assembly Configuration

The structural foundation of the device is established through a housing assembly that integrates four key components: a clutch housing, a clutch connecting portion, a clutch hub, and a disk housing. These elements are interconnected in a manner that collectively defines an internal mounting space, which serves as the primary chamber for housing the friction engagement components. This assembly not only provides structural support but also ensures proper alignment and containment of the internal mechanisms, facilitating smooth operational integration with the rest of the power transmission system.

## Friction Disk Arrangement

Within the mounting space created by the housing assembly, the invention incorporates an alternating series of first and second friction disks. The first friction disks are splined directly to the disk housing, while the second friction disks are splined to the power transmission hub. This alternating arrangement allows the disks to engage and disengage in a coordinated manner, enabling controlled torque transfer between the housing and the hub. The spline connections ensure that rotational forces are effectively transmitted while permitting axial movement necessary for engagement and disengagement.

## Piston Module and Hydraulic Actuation

Central to the invention is a piston module comprising multiple pistons, each paired with its own dedicated piston chamber. This module operates using hydraulic pressure to generate the axial force required to frictionally couple the first and second friction disks. By distributing the engagement force across two or more pistons rather than relying on a single piston, the device achieves more uniform pressure distribution across the friction disk stack, resulting in smoother engagement, reduced wear, and improved torque capacity. The hydraulic pressure supplied to each piston chamber can be independently or collectively regulated, offering enhanced control over the timing and intensity of the clutch engagement process.

## Return Mechanism and Friction Material

To ensure proper disengagement of the friction disks once hydraulic pressure is released, the invention incorporates return springs or separating springs. These springs may be positioned either internally or externally relative to the piston module, depending on the specific design configuration and space constraints of the application. Their primary function is to counteract the axial force generated by the hydraulic pressure, effectively pushing the pistons back to their disengaged position and separating the friction disks when the clutch is not actively engaged.

Furthermore, friction material is strategically applied to the surfaces of the friction disks. This material enhances the frictional coefficient between the first and second friction disks, ensuring efficient torque transfer during engagement while also contributing to the durability and heat resistance of the disks under repeated operational cycles.

## Summary

This multi-piston power transmission device represents a significant advancement in clutch engagement technology, offering improved control, efficiency, and durability through its distributed piston architecture, well-integrated housing assembly, and carefully engineered friction disk and spring return mechanisms.

# Power Transmission Device with Multi-Piston Clutch Assembly

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to power transmission devices, and more particularly to a clutch assembly incorporating multiple pistons for improved engagement and disengagement control in mechanical power transmission systems such as those used in automotive transmissions, industrial machinery, and other torque-transfer applications.

## Background

Conventional clutch assemblies typically utilize a single piston to actuate a friction disk pack, applying hydraulic pressure across the entire disk stack simultaneously. While functional, such single-piston designs often suffer from limitations including uneven pressure distribution across the friction disks, imprecise engagement timing, increased wear on friction materials due to uneven loading, and reduced efficiency during shift transitions. These shortcomings can lead to harsher engagement, increased heat generation, and diminished component longevity.

There exists a need in the art for a clutch assembly design that provides more granular control over the engagement process, allows for more uniform force distribution across friction surfaces, and improves overall power transmission efficiency and smoothness.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these needs by providing a power transmission device utilizing a multi-piston clutch assembly configured to deliver enhanced control over clutch engagement and disengagement operations.

In one aspect, the invention comprises a housing structure that encloses a plurality of friction disks arranged in an alternating configuration. This configuration includes first friction disks operatively connected to a disk housing and second friction disks operatively connected to a power transmission hub. The alternating arrangement ensures that torque can be selectively transmitted between the disk housing and the power transmission hub when the friction disks are brought into engagement with one another.

Engagement of the friction disks is achieved through a piston module comprising multiple pistons, each operable under hydraulic pressure. Unlike conventional single-piston designs, the multi-piston configuration of the present invention allows for staged, distributed, or independently controlled application of clamping force across the friction disk pack. This enables more refined modulation of the engagement process, allowing for smoother torque transfer and reduced mechanical shock during clutch actuation.

To further enhance operational performance, the clutch assembly incorporates return springs, alternatively referred to as separating springs, positioned to counteract the axial forces generated by the hydraulic pistons. These springs serve to reliably disengage the pistons from the friction disk pack when hydraulic pressure is released, ensuring positive separation of the friction disks and preventing unwanted drag or partial engagement during disengaged states. The springs are calibrated to provide sufficient restoring force to overcome residual hydraulic pressure and any adhesive tendencies of the friction material without impeding the engagement process when hydraulic pressure is applied.

Additionally, the friction disks of the present invention are provided with friction material disposed on their respective contact surfaces. This friction material is selected and configured to provide consistent and predictable engagement characteristics, including appropriate coefficients of friction, thermal resistance, and wear characteristics suitable for repeated engagement cycles under varying load and speed conditions.

## Detailed Description

### Housing and Disk Configuration

The housing of the power transmission device serves as the primary structural enclosure for the clutch assembly components. Within this housing, the alternating first and second friction disks are arranged in a stacked configuration, commonly referred to as a disk pack. The first friction disks, connected to the disk housing, may be splined or otherwise mechanically keyed to the interior surface of the housing such that they rotate in unison with the housing while remaining axially movable. Conversely, the second friction disks are connected to the power transmission hub via a complementary splined or keyed connection, allowing these disks to rotate with the hub while similarly retaining axial mobility.

This alternating arrangement of first and second friction disks ensures that, when the disk pack is compressed, torque is transferred from the disk housing through the engaged friction disks to the power transmission hub, or vice versa, depending on the direction of power flow through the system.

### Piston Module and Hydraulic Actuation

The piston module of the present invention is a key innovation, comprising multiple pistons rather than the single piston found in traditional clutch designs. Each piston within the module is configured to receive hydraulic fluid under pressure, which generates an axial force sufficient to compress the friction disk pack and initiate torque transfer.

The use of multiple pistons allows for several advantageous operating modes. In one embodiment, the pistons may be actuated simultaneously to provide a combined clamping force distributed more evenly across the friction disk pack than would be possible with a single larger piston. In another embodiment, the pistons may be actuated sequentially or in a staged manner, allowing for progressive engagement of the clutch, which can reduce engagement shock and improve the smoothness of torque transfer during shifting operations.

The hydraulic circuit supplying pressure to the piston module may include control valves, pressure regulators, and sensors configured to precisely modulate the pressure delivered to each piston, either independently or in coordinated groups, depending on the desired engagement characteristics for a given operating condition.

### Return Spring Mechanism

To ensure reliable disengagement of the clutch assembly when hydraulic pressure is removed, the present invention incorporates one or more return or separating springs. These springs are positioned in operative association with the piston module such that they exert a counteracting force against the hydraulic actuation force generated by the pistons.

When hydraulic pressure is reduced or eliminated, the return springs act to displace the pistons away from the friction disk pack, thereby relieving the compressive force on the friction disks and allowing them to separate. This spring-biased return mechanism helps to prevent clutch drag, reduce parasitic power losses, and improve the overall responsiveness of the clutch assembly during disengagement.

The return springs may be implemented as coil springs, Belleville washers, wave springs, or other suitable elastic elements capable of providing consistent and reliable restoring force over repeated engagement cycles.

### Friction Material Composition

The friction disks of the present invention include friction material applied to their engagement surfaces. This friction material may be composed of organic, paper-based, carbon, ceramic, or sintered metal compositions, selected based on the specific application requirements including torque capacity, operating temperature range, and durability considerations.

The friction material is designed to provide consistent frictional engagement characteristics across the operating life of the clutch assembly, while also facilitating efficient heat dissipation during engagement to minimize thermal degradation of the friction surfaces.

## Advantages of the Invention

The multi-piston clutch assembly of the present invention offers several advantages over conventional single-piston clutch designs, including:

1. **Improved Engagement Precision**: The use of multiple pistons allows for more precise control over the timing and force of clutch engagement, enabling smoother power transmission transitions.

2. **Enhanced Force Distribution**: Distributing hydraulic actuation across multiple pistons allows for more even loading of the friction disk pack, potentially reducing localized wear and extending component life.

3. **Reduced Engagement Shock**: Staged or sequential piston actuation can minimize the mechanical shock associated with clutch engagement, improving ride quality and reducing stress on associated drivetrain components.

4. **Reliable Disengagement**: The incorporation of return springs ensures consistent and positive disengagement of the friction disks, reducing the likelihood of unwanted drag or partial engagement.

5. **Increased Efficiency**: The overall design of the clutch assembly contributes to improved power transmission efficiency by minimizing energy losses associated with incomplete engagement or disengagement events.

## Conclusion

The present invention provides a novel power transmission device utilizing a multi-piston clutch assembly that addresses many of the limitations associated with conventional single-piston clutch designs. Through the combination of alternating friction disks, a multi-piston hydraulic actuation module, return springs, and appropriately configured friction materials, the invention achieves improved precision, efficiency, and reliability in power transmission control applications. Various embodiments and modifications of the disclosed invention will be apparent to those skilled in the art, and it is intended that the scope of the invention be defined by the appended claims rather than the specific embodiments described herein.

# The Word "The"

"The" is one of the most fascinating words in the English language precisely because it seems so unremarkable. As the most frequently used word in English, "the" appears in nearly every sentence we write or speak, yet most of us never stop to consider its function or history.

Grammatically, "the" is known as the definite article. Its job is to signal that we're referring to something specific—a particular object, person, or idea that both the speaker and listener presumably know about. Compare "I saw a dog" (any dog, unspecified) with "I saw the dog" (a specific dog we both know about). This small distinction carries enormous communicative weight.

The word traces its origins back to Old English, evolving from words like "þe" and "se," which were themselves connected to demonstrative pronouns meaning "that" or "this." Over centuries, through the natural evolution of language, these forms simplified into the single word we use today.

Interestingly, not all languages have an equivalent to "the." Russian, Japanese, and many other languages manage perfectly well without definite articles, relying instead on context, word order, or other grammatical markers to convey specificity. This makes "the" a particular challenge for language learners whose native tongues lack this feature.

Despite its small size—just three letters—"the" carries invisible weight in shaping meaning, clarity, and precision in communication. It reminds us that even the most humble words play indispensable roles in the architecture of language.

# PATENT ABSTRACT

## Multi-Piston Power Transmission Clutch Device for Automotive Drivetrains

A multi-piston power transmission clutch device is disclosed for use in automotive drivetrain applications, providing improved torque capacity, engagement control, and packaging efficiency compared to conventional single-piston clutch assemblies. The device comprises a clutch housing defining a plurality of independently actuated hydraulic piston chambers arranged in a coaxial or side-by-side configuration, each chamber housing a corresponding piston operably coupled to a friction plate pack. A hydraulic control circuit selectively and independently pressurizes each piston chamber, enabling staged, sequential, or simultaneous engagement of the friction plates to modulate torque transfer between an input member and an output member of the drivetrain.

Each piston is supported by a return spring mechanism and sealed via elastomeric seal assemblies to prevent hydraulic fluid leakage between adjacent chambers. The friction plate pack includes alternating friction and separator plates splined respectively to the clutch housing and an inner hub member, such that compressive engagement force generated by the multiple pistons is distributed across the plate pack to reduce localized wear and thermal loading during torque transmission events.

In an exemplary embodiment, the multi-piston arrangement permits independent control of engagement force at differing radial positions or plate groupings, allowing for variable torque capacity modulation suited to varying drivetrain load conditions, including launch, shift, and torque-vectoring operations. A control module, in communication with vehicle sensors, regulates hydraulic pressure supplied to each piston chamber based on operating parameters such as engine torque, wheel speed, and gear selection, thereby optimizing clutch engagement smoothness and reducing shift shock.

The disclosed device further includes a lubrication and cooling passage network integrated within the housing and piston assemblies to dissipate heat generated during slip engagement, enhancing durability and thermal stability under repeated actuation cycles. The multi-piston clutch device is adaptable for use in automatic transmissions, dual-clutch transmissions, limited-slip differentials, and hybrid/electric vehicle torque management systems, providing a compact, high-capacity, and precisely controllable power transmission solution.

---

*Note: This is a template/draft abstract suitable for adaptation. A patent professional should tailor specific claims, reference numerals, and technical details to match actual engineering drawings and the specific inventive features of your device before filing.*

# Wet Clutch Assembly with Multiple Pistons, Friction Disks, and Return Springs

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to power transmission devices, and more particularly to a wet clutch assembly employing multiple hydraulically actuated pistons, a friction disk pack, and associated return spring mechanisms for selectively coupling and decoupling rotational power between a driving member and a driven member in a lubricated environment.

---

## Background

Wet clutch assemblies are commonly employed in automotive transmissions, industrial gearboxes, and off-highway equipment to transmit torque through the frictional engagement of interleaved disks operating in a lubricating fluid bath. The lubricant serves to dissipate heat generated during engagement and slip conditions, extend component life, and provide smoother engagement characteristics compared to dry clutch systems.

Conventional single-piston wet clutch designs, while functionally adequate, present limitations with respect to actuation force distribution, response time, and packaging within increasingly compact transmission housings. A single piston acting upon an extended friction disk stack may produce uneven axial loading across the disk pack, leading to non-uniform wear, localized hot spots, and reduced torque capacity for a given envelope size. Additionally, single-piston designs typically require larger piston diameters or higher hydraulic pressures to achieve requisite clamping force, which can increase component stress and reduce durability.

There exists a need for a wet clutch assembly that distributes actuation forces more evenly across a friction disk pack, provides improved response and release characteristics, and permits more compact axial packaging while maintaining or improving torque transmission capacity.

---

## Summary

The present disclosure provides a wet clutch assembly comprising a clutch housing defining a fluid-tight actuation chamber, at least two axially movable pistons disposed within the housing, a friction disk pack comprising a plurality of alternating friction disks and separator disks, and at least one return spring assembly configured to bias each piston toward a disengaged position. The pistons are hydraulically actuated, independently or in coordinated fashion, to apply axial clamping force to discrete portions of the friction disk pack, thereby engaging the clutch. Upon removal of hydraulic pressure, the return springs urge the pistons to their retracted positions, releasing the friction disk pack and disengaging the clutch.

In certain embodiments, the multiple pistons act upon separate axial segments of a single friction disk pack, or alternatively upon two or more independently arranged friction disk packs, permitting staged or segmented engagement. The use of multiple pistons allows for reduced individual piston diameter, lower peak hydraulic pressure requirements, and more uniform distribution of clamping load across the friction disk pack, which is expected to improve wear characteristics and thermal management relative to single-piston designs.

---

## Detailed Description

### 1. General Arrangement

Referring to the assembly generally, the wet clutch comprises:

- **(10)** A clutch housing/drum, rotatable about a central axis and defining an internal cavity;
- **(20a, 20b)** A first piston and a second piston, each slidably received within respective annular piston bores formed in or coupled to the housing;
- **(30)** A friction disk pack comprising alternating friction disks (splined to an inner hub or shaft) and separator/reaction plates (splined to the outer housing or drum);
- **(40a, 40b)** A first return spring assembly and a second return spring assembly, each associated with a respective piston;
- **(50)** A pressure plate or backing plate against which the friction disk pack is compressed;
- **(60)** Hydraulic fluid supply passages and control valving for delivering pressurized actuation fluid to each piston chamber;
- **(70)** Lubrication fluid passages for supplying cooling/lubricating oil to the friction disk pack during operation.

### 2. Piston Configuration

The first piston (20a) is disposed within a first annular actuation chamber formed within the clutch housing, while the second piston (20b) is disposed within a second annular actuation chamber, axially and/or radially offset from the first chamber. In one embodiment, the two pistons are arranged in a nested, concentric configuration, wherein the second piston is positioned radially inward or outward of the first piston, both pistons acting in the same axial direction upon the friction disk pack or upon separate friction disk packs.

In an alternative embodiment, the pistons are arranged in axial series, wherein the first piston acts upon a first portion of the friction disk pack and the second piston acts upon a second, axially adjacent portion of the friction disk pack, the two portions being separated by an intermediate reaction plate common to both piston actuation zones.

Each piston includes a sealing arrangement, such as one or more elastomeric or composite seals (e.g., lip seals or O-rings) disposed in grooves formed in the piston body and/or bore wall, to maintain fluid separation between the actuation chamber and adjacent lubrication or ambient regions.

Hydraulic fluid is supplied to each piston's respective actuation chamber via dedicated fluid passages formed in the housing, shaft, or an intermediate stationary member, such passages being in fluid communication with a transmission control valve body. In certain embodiments, the two piston chambers may be supplied from a common pressure source through a shared passage with a flow-splitting or balancing orifice, or alternatively from independently controlled solenoid valves, permitting differential or sequential actuation of the pistons.

### 3. Friction Disk Pack

The friction disk pack (30) comprises a plurality of friction disks interleaved with separator plates. The friction disks are provided with a friction material lining (e.g., paper-based, carbon, or sintered bronze composite) bonded or mechanically affixed to one or both faces, and are splined for rotation with an inner member (such as a clutch hub connected to an input or output shaft). The separator plates are typically fabricated from hardened steel and splined for rotation with the clutch housing or drum.

In the multi-piston configuration, the friction disk pack may be divided into two or more axial groups, each group being compressed by a respective piston. This segmentation allows the total clamping load required for a given torque capacity to be shared between multiple pistons, reducing the load, and consequently the required diameter or hydraulic pressure, for each individual piston.

Alternatively, a single, undivided friction disk pack may be engaged by both pistons acting in a coordinated fashion, wherein the first piston provides a majority of the clamping force through a larger actuation area and applies a preliminary or "priming" force, and the second piston provides a supplemental or fine-tuning force. This arrangement facilitates smoother clutch engagement by allowing a two-stage or graduated force application, reducing engagement shock.

### 4. Return Spring Assemblies

Each piston is biased toward its disengaged (retracted) position by a dedicated return spring assembly (40a, 40b). In a preferred embodiment, each return spring assembly comprises a plurality of coil compression springs arranged circumferentially about the clutch axis and retained between the respective piston and a spring retainer plate, the retainer plate being secured to the housing by a snap ring or similar retaining feature.

In an alternative embodiment, the return spring assembly comprises one or more Belleville (disk) springs, or a wave spring, disposed to act between the piston and a fixed reaction surface. The use of Belleville springs may be advantageous where axial packaging space is limited, as such springs can provide the requisite return force within a reduced axial envelope compared to coil springs.

The spring rate and preload of each return spring assembly may be selected independently, such that the first and second pistons exhibit different release characteristics, timing, or force profiles, thereby enabling tailored engagement and disengagement sequencing between the two piston-actuated clamping zones.

### 5. Lubrication and Cooling

Lubricating fluid is supplied to the friction disk pack through radial and/or axial passages (70) formed in the clutch hub, shaft, or housing, such fluid being distributed across the friction disk faces during both engaged and disengaged operation to dissipate frictional heat and reduce wear. In certain embodiments, one or more of the pistons or separator plates include flow channels or apertures to promote fluid circulation through the disk pack interstices.

### 6. Operation

In operation, hydraulic fluid under pressure is admitted to the first and/or second piston actuation chambers via the associated control valve(s). The resulting hydraulic force acting on the piston area overcomes the opposing force of the respective return spring assembly, causing the piston(s) to translate axially and compress the friction disk pack (or respective disk pack segments) against the pressure plate. Frictional engagement between the friction disks and separator plates thereby couples the input and output members for torque transmission.

Upon reduction or removal of hydraulic pressure, the return spring assemblies drive the pistons back to their retracted positions, relieving the clamping force on the friction disk pack and permitting relative rotational slip between the input and output members, thereby disengaging the clutch.

In embodiments employing independently controllable pistons, the transmission control system may selectively actuate the first piston, the second piston, or both in a coordinated sequence, to achieve variable engagement force profiles, staged engagement (e.g., for shift quality management in multi-speed transmissions), or redundancy in the event of a fault condition affecting one hydraulic circuit.

---

## Advantages

- Distribution of clamping load across multiple pistons reduces per-piston diameter and/or hydraulic pressure requirements for a given torque capacity.
- Improved uniformity of axial loading across the friction disk pack, reducing localized wear and hot-spotting.
- Enables staged or graduated engagement profiles for improved shift quality and reduced engagement shock.
- Facilitates compact axial packaging through use of nested or segmented piston arrangements.
- Provides potential for redundant actuation paths, improving robustness against single-point hydraulic failures.

---

## Illustrative Claims (Representative)

1. A wet clutch assembly comprising: a housing defining a rotational axis; a first piston and a second piston each slidably disposed within the housing and axially movable relative thereto; a friction disk pack comprising a plurality of interleaved friction disks and separator plates disposed to be selectively compressed by at least one of the first piston and the second piston; a first return spring assembly configured to bias the first piston toward a disengaged position; and a second return spring assembly configured to bias the second piston toward a disengaged position; wherein the first piston and the second piston are each responsive to hydraulic pressure supplied to a respective actuation chamber to compress at least a portion of the friction disk pack.

2. The wet clutch assembly of claim 1, wherein the first piston and the second piston are arranged concentrically, one of the first piston and the second piston being disposed radially inward of the other.

3. The wet clutch assembly of claim 1, wherein the friction disk pack comprises a first disk pack segment compressible by the first piston and a second disk pack segment compressible by the second piston, the first and second disk pack segments being axially adjacent.

4. The wet clutch assembly of claim 1, wherein at least one of the first return spring assembly and the second return spring assembly comprises a plurality of circumferentially arranged coil compression springs.

5. The wet clutch assembly of claim 1, wherein at least one of the first return spring assembly and the second return spring assembly comprises a Belleville spring.

6. The wet clutch assembly of claim 1, further comprising a control system configured to selectively supply hydraulic pressure to the first piston and the second piston independently of one another.

---

*Note: This description is presented in a generalized format suitable for adaptation to a specific implementation. Actual patent claims should be drafted and reviewed by a qualified patent attorney to ensure adequate scope, novelty, and compliance with applicable patent office requirements, and should be tailored to the specific inventive features and prior art landscape relevant to the actual invention.*

# Patent-Style Description: Vehicle Clutch Mechanism

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to power transmission systems for vehicles, and more particularly to a clutch mechanism comprising a housing assembly, a piston module, and a friction disk arrangement configured to selectively engage and disengage rotational power transfer between a driving member and a driven member.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with one embodiment, a clutch mechanism is provided comprising:

**(a) a housing** defining an internal cavity and having a substantially cylindrical inner wall, the housing including a first end wall and an opposing second end wall, at least one of the end walls defining a fluid inlet port in fluid communication with the internal cavity;

**(b) a piston module** slidably disposed within the internal cavity of the housing, the piston module comprising a piston body having a first face and an opposing second face, the first face defining a pressure chamber in cooperation with the first end wall of the housing, the piston module further including at least one sealing member disposed circumferentially about the piston body to sealingly engage the inner wall of the housing, wherein the piston module is configured to translate axially within the housing responsive to a fluid pressure differential introduced through the fluid inlet port; and

**(c) a friction disk arrangement** positioned within the internal cavity adjacent the second face of the piston body, the friction disk arrangement comprising a plurality of first friction disks operatively coupled to a driving shaft and a plurality of second friction disks interleaved with the first friction disks and operatively coupled to a driven shaft, wherein axial translation of the piston module urges the plurality of first friction disks into frictional engagement with the plurality of second friction disks to transmit rotational torque between the driving shaft and the driven shaft.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### The Housing Assembly

Referring generally to the figures, a clutch mechanism **100** is disclosed. The clutch mechanism **100** includes a housing **110** configured to enclose and support the operative components of the clutch mechanism **100**. The housing **110** comprises a generally cylindrical body **112** defining an internal cavity **114** therein. The housing **110** further comprises a first end wall **116** and a second end wall **118** disposed in axially spaced relation to one another, the first and second end walls **116**, **118** cooperating with the cylindrical body **112** to enclose the internal cavity **114**.

The first end wall **116** defines at least one fluid inlet port **120** extending therethrough, the fluid inlet port **120** being in fluid communication with the internal cavity **114** to permit the introduction of a pressurized hydraulic or pneumatic fluid therein. In certain embodiments, the housing **110** further defines a fluid outlet port **122** disposed in spaced relation to the fluid inlet port **120**, the fluid outlet port **122** facilitating the evacuation of fluid from the internal cavity **114** during a disengagement operation.

The housing **110** may further comprise a mounting flange **124** extending radially outward from the cylindrical body **112**, the mounting flange **124** defining a plurality of apertures **126** configured to receive a corresponding plurality of fasteners for securing the housing **110** to a transmission casing or other structural component of the vehicle.

### The Piston Module

Disposed within the internal cavity **114** of the housing **110** is a piston module **130**. The piston module **130** comprises a piston body **132** having a first face **134** and an opposing second face **136**. The first face **134** of the piston body **132**, in cooperation with the first end wall **116** of the housing **110**, defines a pressure chamber **138** therebetween.

The piston body **132** further comprises an inner circumferential surface **140** and an outer circumferential surface **142**, the outer circumferential surface **142** being configured to slidably and sealingly engage the inner wall **113** of the cylindrical body **112**. At least one sealing member **144**, such as an O-ring or lip seal, is disposed within a corresponding annular groove **146** formed in the outer circumferential surface **142** of the piston body **132**, the sealing member **144** being configured to prevent fluid leakage from the pressure chamber **138** during operation.

# Summary of the Invention

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to power transmission devices, and more particularly to a hydraulically actuated clutch or brake assembly employing multiple pistons, splined friction disks, and separating springs for improved engagement and disengagement performance in automotive or industrial drivetrains.

## Background Considerations Addressed

Conventional power transmission devices utilizing friction disk assemblies often suffer from drag torque losses during disengagement, uneven load distribution across friction elements, and premature wear due to inconsistent disk separation. There exists a need for an improved apparatus that ensures reliable separation of friction disks when not engaged, while providing robust and efficient torque transfer when engaged.

## Summary of the Invention

In accordance with the present invention, a power transmission device is provided comprising a housing defining a chamber, a plurality of friction disks disposed within the chamber, and a plurality of pistons operatively associated with the friction disks to selectively apply and release compressive engagement forces thereon.

The friction disks include a set of splined outer disks and a set of splined inner disks, the splined outer disks being engaged with corresponding splines formed on an interior surface of the housing, and the splined inner disks being engaged with corresponding splines formed on an outer surface of a rotatable hub or shaft disposed within the housing. The splined engagement permits axial movement of the disks relative to the housing and hub while constraining relative rotational movement, thereby enabling torque transmission when the disks are placed in frictional contact with one another.

The plurality of pistons are arranged to be actuated by a source of hydraulic or pneumatic pressure, and are configured to apply an axial clamping force against the stacked arrangement of splined outer and inner disks, thereby compressing the disks into frictional engagement to transmit torque between the housing and the hub. In one aspect, the pistons may be arranged in a stacked or tandem configuration to provide increased clamping force while maintaining a compact axial envelope, or may be distributed circumferentially to provide balanced loading across the disk pack.

A plurality of separating springs are further provided, each spring being disposed and configured to bias the friction disks apart from one another in the absence of an applied piston force. The separating springs act between adjacent disks, or between a disk and an adjacent reaction plate or piston face, to establish and maintain a predetermined separation gap between the friction surfaces when the device is in a disengaged state. This arrangement advantageously minimizes drag torque and associated parasitic losses, reduces wear on the friction material, and promotes rapid and consistent disengagement response.

In one embodiment, the separating springs comprise wave springs or coil springs retained within recesses or apertures formed in the disks or in an associated retaining structure, such that the springs are captured and properly aligned during both the engaged and disengaged conditions of the device. In another embodiment, the separating springs are configured to provide a progressively increasing return force as the disks are compressed, thereby aiding in rapid and uniform disk separation upon release of the piston-applied force.

The plurality of pistons may be hydraulically interconnected such that fluid pressure is distributed substantially evenly among the pistons, ensuring uniform application of clamping force across the friction disk pack and thereby promoting even wear and consistent torque capacity over the operational life of the device. Alternatively, the pistons may be independently controllable to permit selective or staged engagement of different portions of the friction disk pack, allowing for variable torque transmission characteristics depending on operating conditions.

The combination of the splined friction disk arrangement, the multiple-piston actuation system, and the separating spring assembly provides a power transmission device that achieves efficient, reliable, and rapid engagement and disengagement, with reduced drag losses, improved thermal management due to enhanced disk separation and airflow, and extended service life relative to conventional friction clutch and brake assemblies.

Additional features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become apparent from the following detailed description and accompanying drawings, which illustrate, by way of example, the principles of the invention.

# CLUTCH HOUSING ASSEMBLY WITH ALTERNATING FRICTION DISK ENGAGEMENT

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to power transmission devices, and more particularly to a clutch housing assembly comprising a plurality of alternating first and second friction disks selectively engageable via a hydraulically actuated piston chamber arrangement for transmitting rotational torque between a drive member and a driven member.

---

## BACKGROUND

Multi-disk clutch assemblies are commonly employed in automotive transmissions, industrial machinery, and power take-off systems to selectively couple and decouple rotating shafts. Conventional designs often suffer from inconsistent engagement pressure distribution across the friction disk stack, resulting in uneven wear, reduced torque capacity, and premature failure of friction材料 (friction material). There exists a need for a clutch assembly that provides uniform axial clamping force across an alternating disk stack while minimizing hydraulic fluid volume and response time.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

According to one embodiment, a clutch housing assembly is provided comprising:

1. A housing member defining an internal cavity and a hydraulic fluid passage;
2. A plurality of first friction disks rotationally coupled to an input shaft or drum, said first disks having splined outer or inner peripheral edges;
3. A plurality of second friction disks rotationally coupled to an output hub, said second disks interleaved in alternating sequence with the first friction disks to form a friction disk pack;
4. A piston assembly disposed within the housing and defining a hydraulic piston chamber, the piston being axially translatable in response to pressurized hydraulic fluid introduced into the chamber;
5. A return mechanism, such as a Belleville spring or coil spring array, configured to bias the piston to a disengaged position upon release of hydraulic pressure;
6. A pressure plate or reaction plate positioned at a terminal end of the friction disk pack opposite the piston, against which the disk pack is compressed.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### 1. General Structure

Referring to the accompanying figures (not shown herein but referenced as FIG. 1–FIG. 4 in the formal filing), the clutch housing assembly (**10**) comprises a generally cylindrical housing (**12**) having a first axial end (**14**) and a second axial end (**16**). The housing (**12**) defines an internal chamber (**18**) sized to receive a friction disk pack (**20**).

### 2. Friction Disk Pack Configuration

The friction disk pack (**20**) comprises a plurality of **first friction disks (22)** and a plurality of **second friction disks (24)** arranged in an alternating axial sequence such that each first friction disk (22) is positioned axially between two second friction disks (24), and vice versa, with the exception of the terminal disks at each end of the stack.

- **First friction disks (22)** include a plurality of splines (**22a**) formed along an outer circumferential edge, said splines (22a) engaging complementary splines (**26**) formed on an interior surface of a drive drum (**28**) rotationally coupled to an input shaft (**30**). This engagement permits axial sliding movement of the first friction disks (22) relative to the drive drum (28) while constraining relative rotation.

- **Second friction disks (24)** include a plurality of splines (**24a**) formed along an inner circumferential edge, said splines (24a) engaging complementary splines (**32**) formed on an outer surface of a driven hub (**34**) coupled to an output shaft (**36**). Similarly, the second friction disks (24) are axially slidable relative to the driven hub (34) but rotationally fixed thereto.

Each of the first friction disks (22) and second friction disks (24) may include a friction lining (**38**) affixed to one or both major faces thereof, said friction lining (38) comprising a paper-based, carbon-based, or ceramic composite material selected to provide a defined coefficient of friction and thermal resistance.

### 3. Piston and Hydraulic Actuation System

A piston (**40**) is slidably received within a piston bore (**42**) formed in the housing (**12**), said piston (**40**) and piston bore (**42**) cooperatively defining a **hydraulic piston chamber (44)**. The hydraulic piston chamber (44) is in fluid communication with a hydraulic fluid supply passage (**46**) formed within the housing (12) and/or a rotating shaft, said passage (46) being connected to an external or internal hydraulic pump (not shown) via a control valve assembly.

Upon introduction of pressurized hydraulic fluid into the hydraulic piston chamber (44), the piston (40) is displaced axially in a first direction (indicated by arrow **A** in FIG. 2) toward the friction disk pack (20). The piston (40) contacts an apply plate (**48**), which in turn transmits axial force sequentially through the alternating first friction disks (22) and second friction disks (24), compressing the friction disk pack (20) against the reaction plate (**50**) fixed at the opposing end of the housing (12).

The resulting compressive force generates frictional engagement between adjacent first friction disks (22) and second friction disks (24), thereby coupling the drive drum (28) to the driven hub (34) such that torque is transmitted from the input shaft (30) to the output shaft (36).

### 4. Return Mechanism

Upon release of hydraulic pressure within the hydraulic piston chamber (44), a return spring (**52**), which may comprise a Belleville washer, wave spring, or a plurality of coil springs arranged circumferentially about the piston (40), urges the piston (40) axially in a second direction opposite arrow A, thereby releasing the compressive force on the friction disk pack (20) and disengaging the clutch.

### 5. Sealing and Fluid Retention

A plurality of sealing elements (**54, 56**), such as O-rings or lip seals, are disposed between the piston (40) and the piston bore (42), and between the piston (40) and a central shaft or sleeve, to prevent hydraulic fluid leakage from the hydraulic piston chamber (44) during pressurization.

Optionally, a centrifugal balance chamber (**58**) may be defined on an opposing side of the piston (40) to counteract centrifugal hydraulic pressure effects generated during high-speed rotation of the housing (12), said balance chamber (58) being vented or supplied with lubricating fluid at a substantially constant low pressure.

### 6. Lubrication

A lubrication passage (**60**) may be formed through the driven hub (34) and/or drive drum (28) to deliver lubricating fluid to the friction disk pack (20), reducing thermal buildup and facilitating smooth separation of the first friction disks (22) and second friction disks (24) upon disengagement.

---

## OPERATION

In operation, the clutch housing assembly (10) functions as follows:

1. **Disengaged State:** In the absence of hydraulic pressure in chamber (44), the return spring (52) maintains the piston (40) in a retracted position, and the friction disk pack (20) remains uncompressed, permitting free relative rotation between the drive drum (28) and driven hub (34).

2. **Engagement Initiation:** A control valve directs pressurized hydraulic fluid into the hydraulic piston chamber (44) via passage (46), generating a hydraulic force on the piston (40) that exceeds the biasing force of the return spring (52).

3. **Compression Phase:** The piston (40) advances axially, applying force through the apply plate (48) and progressively compressing the alternating first friction disks (22) and second friction disks (24) against the reaction plate (50).

4. **Torque Transmission:** Frictional contact between adjacent disk faces enables torque transfer from the input shaft (30) through the drive drum (28), across the friction disk pack (20), to the driven hub (34) and output shaft (36).

5. **Disengagement:** Upon reduction or removal of hydraulic pressure, the return spring (52) forces the piston (40) back to its initial position, separating the friction disks (22, 24) and interrupting torque transmission.

---

## CLAIMS (Exemplary)

**Claim 1.** A clutch housing assembly comprising:
a housing defining a hydraulic piston chamber;
a drive drum rotationally coupled to an input shaft;
a driven hub rotationally coupled to an output shaft;
a plurality of first friction disks splined to said drive drum;
a plurality of second friction disks splined to said driven hub and arranged in alternating axial sequence with said first friction disks to form a friction disk pack;
a piston slidably disposed within said hydraulic piston chamber and configured to apply axial compressive force to said friction disk pack upon introduction of pressurized hydraulic fluid into said chamber; and
a return spring configured to bias said piston away from said friction disk pack upon release of said hydraulic pressure.

**Claim 2.** The clutch housing assembly of claim 1, wherein said first friction disks and said second friction disks each comprise a friction lining affixed to at least one major face thereof.

**Claim 3.** The clutch housing assembly of claim 1, further comprising a centrifugal balance chamber disposed on a side of said piston opposite said hydraulic piston chamber, configured to counteract centrifugal pressure effects during rotation.

**Claim 4.** The clutch housing assembly of claim 1, further comprising a lubrication passage formed in at least one of said drive drum and said driven hub, configured to deliver lubricating fluid to said friction disk pack.

**Claim 5.** The clutch housing assembly of claim 1, wherein said return spring comprises a Belleville washer disposed circumferentially about said piston.

**Claim 6.** The clutch housing assembly of claim 1, wherein said hydraulic fluid passage is formed at least partially within a rotating shaft in fluid communication with said input shaft.

---
